item.title: Tribunal upholds $10K fine for B.C. ostrich farm over failure to report sick birds
item.description: The Canada Agricultural Review Tribunal has upheld a $10,000 fine handed to the British Columbia ostrich farm whose flock of more than 300 birds was culled last fall, nearly 11 months after the confirmation of an avian influenza outbreak.

item.title: Government's use of Emergencies Act in 2022 was 'unreasonable': Court of Appeal
item.description: OTTAWA — The Federal Court of Appeal has ruled it was unreasonable for the Liberal government to use the Emergencies Act four years ago to quell protests in the national capital and at key border points.

item.title: 'Damn excited': Calgary lifts water-use restrictions after broken pipe repaired
item.description: CALGARY — Calgary’s 1.6 million residents and those in surrounding municipalities are once again free to flush and take longer showers, as water restrictions imposed due to a broken water main were lifted Friday.

item.title: Killer of Lapu Lapu suspect's brother calls festival attack a 'ripple effect'
item.description: VANCOUVER — The murderer of a man whose brother was later arrested for the Lapu Lapu festival attack that killed 11 people in Vancouver last April has called it a "ripple effect" from his own crime 15 months earlier.

item.title: Insured flood costs estimated at $74M in B.C.'s Fraser Valley
item.description: Severe weather and flooding that lashed southern British Columbia and parts of Alberta last month caused close to $90 million in insured damage, with B.C.'s Fraser Valley suffering the heaviest losses, the Insurance Bureau of Canada said Friday.

item.title: Carney reaches 'landmark' tariff quota deal with China on EVs, canola
item.description: BEIJING — Prime Minister Mark Carney touted a renewed relationship with China and "enormous progress" on trade irritants as he announced a new deal with Beijing on electric vehicles and canola at the end of a high-profile trip to China on Friday.

item.title: Canadian official says Carney will accept role on Trump's Gaza 'Board of Peace'
item.description: BEIJING — A senior Canadian government official says Prime Minister Mark Carney has been asked by U.S. President Donald Trump to join the "Board of Peace" tasked with supporting the administration, reconstruction and economic recovery of Gaza.
